v2_findings.title: WC — Stop Gap for Monopolistic States
v2_findings.content:
[Good] WC — Stop Gap for Monopolistic States

What this means:
There are four states (North Dakota, Ohio, Washington, Wyoming) that require workers' comp from a state fund — your private policy can't write WC there. But your private policy DOES include 'stop gap' employers' liability coverage in those four states, so if an employee gets injured there and sues,

Recommendation:
Maintain. Confirm any expansion into those states is reported.

v2_findings.content:

Risk Score: 9/25

Your workers' comp policy has a blanket waiver of subrogation that applies in 9 states plus California separately — but not in Georgia, North Carolina, or Illinois, where you also have employees. v2_findings.title: Workers' Comp — Experience Modification Rate
v2_findings.content:
[Good] Workers' Comp — Experience Modification Rate

What this means:
Your workers' comp experience modifier is 0.69 — meaning you have 31% fewer losses than the industry average for your work. That's excellent. It saves you real money and signals to county clients that you run a safe operation.

Recommendation:
Maintain safety culture. Use the favorable EMR as a competitive differentiator in RFP responses (many counties require EMR ≤ 1.0).
